title: Atomic local SQLite and filesystem-CAS publication

expected_red.precondition: The future TDD branch contains only the black-box S3 harness and reviewed storage fixture while production remains at merged S2 behavior.
expected_red.runner_expected_exit: nonzero because the acceptance assertion fails
expected_red.accepted_reason: Merged S2 parses the full S3 invocation before profile validation and rejects the unknown --store pair as input.invalid_revision, so no durable head can exist.
rejected_reasons: probe failure outside a named boundary

failure_precedence: store root, marker, schema, and path validation
CAS staging in canonical artifact order

scenarios.arrange: Materialize the reviewed A/B Git history, an external empty store root, fixed repository identity, and independent process probe.
scenarios.act: Publish A, restart and read A, publish B, restart and read B, then retry B.
assert: Each successful scan emits the unchanged reviewed RepositorySnapshotV3 and empty stderr.
Every restart returns one complete hash-valid reviewed LocalSnapshotHeadV1.
The B retry creates no duplicate immutable row or object and does not increase head generation.

scenarios.arrange: Apply the same metadata contract vectors to the deterministic fake and real SQLite WAL adapter.
scenarios.act: Open, insert immutable snapshot rows, compare/set heads, read, contend, reopen, and inject typed failures.
assert: Fake and SQLite expose the same domain results and failure precedence.
Only project_heads mutates; every other reviewed row rejects update and delete.
Unknown schema, foreign-key violation, writer contention, and metadata corruption fail closed.

scenarios.arrange: Apply the same exact-byte vectors to the deterministic fake and real filesystem CAS adapter.
scenarios.act: Stage new, existing-identical, short-write, mismatched-existing, missing, corrupted, and orphan objects.
assert: Artifact IDs, lengths, reuse, and typed failures match the shared contract.
No final path exposes partial bytes and an existing object is never overwritten.
The real adapter writes only below the explicit store root.

scenarios.arrange: For each ratified boundary occurrence, prepare both first publication and A-to-B replacement in fresh stores; exercise every canonical artifact occurrence for CAS boundaries.
scenarios.act: Terminate the probe externally at the exact boundary, restart, read, retry, sweep, and read again.
assert: Pre-commit termination exposes none or A exactly as reviewed; post-commit termination exposes A or B exactly as reviewed.
No partial or mixed head is ever returned.
Every retry and sweep converges to the reviewed complete head without deleting reachable bytes.

scenarios.arrange: Generate bounded schedules of reader transactions around each publication transition.
scenarios.act: Interleave reads before begin, during immutable inserts, after uncommitted head update, and after commit.
assert: Every reader observes exactly no head, A, or B according to transaction boundaries.
No schedule constructs a head from rows or objects belonging to different snapshots.
The model and both fake/real adapters agree.

scenarios.arrange: Generate duplicate and interrupted deliveries of the same repository identity and snapshot ID.
scenarios.act: Retry each sequence up to the reviewed count with no hidden adapter retry.
assert: One semantic snapshot has one immutable row set and one artifact set.
Publishing the current head does not increment generation.
Conflicting expected heads fail retryably without overwriting a committed head.

scenarios.arrange: Publish each reviewed head using the real SQLite and filesystem adapters.
scenarios.act: Drop every handle, start a new process, reopen the marker and schema, and load by repository identity.
assert: The exact snapshot ID, commit, generation, ordered references, lengths, and hashes survive.
SQLite reports the ratified PRAGMAs and schema identity.
Reopen performs no migration, repair, network call, or repository read.

scenarios.arrange: Create missing, byte-corrupt, wrong-length, wrong-digest, dangling-row, and invalid-schema variants from a reviewed store.
scenarios.act: Restart and load the visible head.
assert: Every reachable corruption returns the reviewed typed V4 error with empty stdout.
The adapter never falls back to an older head or returns degraded success.
Public errors expose bounded identifiers and never absolute paths or object bytes.

scenarios.arrange: Create reviewed pre-commit orphans, abandoned temporary files, decoy digest paths, and one complete B head.
scenarios.act: Run bounded sweep with schedule permutations and crash/restart around deletion.
assert: Every head-reachable object is reverified and retained.
Only objects absent from a stable committed reachability view are deleted.
The B head remains complete and byte-identical after every schedule.

scenarios.arrange: Prepare overlap, symlink or reparse, unmarked nonempty, traversal, sibling-canary, repository-canary, and valid external-root cases.
scenarios.act: Open or initialize the store and attempt publication.
assert: Unsafe roots fail before mutation with the reviewed redacted V4 error.
Valid publication changes only the marked store root.
Repository, sibling canaries, process count, and network observers remain unchanged.

scenarios.arrange: Load the reviewed DDL, marker, head/error schemas, contract model, and one-field/cross-reference mutations.
scenarios.act: Execute DDL on a fresh database and validate every reviewed and mutated document.
assert: The exact v1 schema, PRAGMAs, tables, foreign keys, immutability triggers, and one mutable head are present.
Missing, unknown, duplicate, reordered, dangling, wrong-version, wrong-hash, and out-of-range values fail.
V4 error stage and retryability are fixed by code.

scenarios.arrange: Run every inherited S0–S2 command and oracle without a store argument.
scenarios.act: Compare stdout, stderr, exit, schemas, semantic bytes, and zero-write observations.
assert: S0/V1, S1/V2, and S2/V3 remain byte-compatible.
Legacy paths create no store and perform no new write.
Only the explicit standard-local-s3 profile may publish.

evidence_contract.red: Retain the first expected failing runner log before production changes, with base and pre-implementation SHAs, runner and subject exits, V2 stderr code, absent store, command, environment, SHA-256, and immutable locator.
evidence_contract.green: Retain one ordered passing result for every S3 scenario and inherited S0–S2 regression, with command, exit, report digest, and immutable locator.
evidence_contract.storage: Retain SQLite version and compile options, PRAGMAs, schema digest, marker digest, row counts, head generations, CAS paths relative to the store, object lengths and digests, and fake/real parity.
evidence_contract.faults: Retain one first-run process trace per named boundary occurrence, exact artifact role and ordinal where applicable, observation signal, termination result, first-publication and replacement restart heads, both corresponding retry heads, sweep result, and raw log digest; retries never replace first evidence.
evidence_contract.durability: Retain OS, filesystem, file-sync, atomic-move, parent-sync, and SQLite-commit primitives and distinguish process-crash evidence from power-loss evidence.
evidence_contract.security: Retain root identities, symlink or reparse decisions, write-set audit, repository/sibling canary hashes, process and network observer self-tests, and redacted errors.
environment: SQLite library version and compile options
evidence_contract.retention: Every required log, database copy, object manifest, report, and minimized reproducer remains retrievable and digest-valid for at least 90 days.
evidence_contract.verification_rule: Local evidence may support review but cannot set Verified without immutable exact-head CI artifacts and honest platform durability evidence.

stop_conditions: The protected contract differs from the approved S3 bundle.
The first product Red is absent or fails for a reason other than standard-local-s3 being rejected by merged S2.
Snapshot or artifact identity, SQLite transaction boundaries, CAS durability, head visibility, path safety, corruption, cleanup reachability, or failpoint outcome is ambiguous.
A platform adapter cannot name a successful file and parent durability primitive but claims durable staging.
A required case can pass only by retrying, repairing, falling back, skipping, or weakening the oracle.
S0–S2 regressions fail or their public dispatch changes.
The task exceeds its allowed paths, high-risk scope, resource budget, or two bounded correction attempts.
